game.title: Game Night Gauntlet
game.description: Dice, cards, tiles and hot takes: a game-night trivia mix for any crowd. No experts required.

images.description: Four letter tiles on a rack spelling QUIZ. Each tile shows its point value: Q 10, U 1, I 1, Z 10.
Five playing cards: king of clubs, 2 of spades, queen of hearts, 3 of hearts, ace of diamonds.
Five playing cards: 9 of clubs, 4 of spades, king of spades, 4 of diamonds, 9 of hearts.
Five playing cards: 8 of spades, 5 of clubs, 9 of clubs, 6 of diamonds, 7 of hearts.
Five playing cards: queen of diamonds, 10 of hearts, 2 of hearts, king of clubs, jack of spades.
About 60 colorful dice scattered across a green table, showing assorted faces.

questions.prompt: Confession time: I have quit a game of Monopoly before it ended.
On a standard six-sided die, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to…
Using the tile values shown (standard English-language Scrabble), what is the base score for QUIZ, with no bonus squares?
Under standard poker rules (no wild cards), which of these hands is a straight?
Which of these games use dice in their standard rules? Select all that apply.
Sort each game by what you mainly play it with.
Find the only die showing a single pip (a one)!
True or false: not counting castling, the knight is the only chess piece that can jump over other pieces.
In chess, the special move in which the king and a rook move on the same turn is called ___.
Love it or leave it? Sort these game-night classics.
